options.description: Close the question: it matches RFC-0021, where a key names an item or a folder, never both, and a flat store's a/a-slash clash is a refusal (A.8). Typed keys stay a recorded alternative in § 6.

options.label: Add typed keys as a model
options.description: A second axiom set over names × {item, folder}, with its own Alloy and Lean restatement. Only worth it if a backend must expose a and a/ at once.

questions.question: § 10 Q2: is finiteness imposed when operations are added?

options.label: Axioms stay infinite (Recommended)
options.description: Close it: the axioms keep no finiteness. The operations model (Dafny map) covers finite stores only, and that limit is stated where operations are specified. The Lean infinite-model results stay valid.

options.label: Add a finiteness axiom
options.description: AX-9: U is finite. Simplifies the operations pass, but excludes the infinite models Lean proved exist, and § 6 and § 9.7 change.

options.label: Decide in the Dafny step
options.description: Leave it open until the operations are written.

questions.question: § 10 Q3: StoreTree.dfy's Key = seq<string> admits "" and "a/b" (against AX-7). Which fix does BK-434 take after #1130 lands?

options.label: Restrict Key's type (Recommended)
options.description: A subset type of non-empty, slash-free segments, so ValidTree satisfies AX-7 by construction and every lemma inherits it. Touches StoreTree.dfy, so it is BK-434's job after Thursday.

options.label: Precondition on callers
options.description: Tree stays permissive, and each operation requires well-formed keys, mirroring the kernel's key validation. Smaller change, but a Tree value can still break AX-7.

questions.question: § 10 Q4 (BK-435's open decision): are the axioms promoted into a spec now that they are proved?

options.label: New store-model spec (Recommended)
options.description: A new sdd/specs/ file stating AX-1..AX-8 with spec IDs, the research doc as its rationale. The spec-mark gate then needs a test mark per section (e.g. conformance checks on key shape and listing prefix-closure), which is real work, but it is what binds a backend.

options.label: Section in spec 003
options.description: Add the axioms to 003-backend-adapter-contract.md. Same test-mark obligation, but it mixes the static model with the operation contract.

options.label: No spec, decide against
options.description: The research doc and formal layers stay the authority, and specs link to them. BK-435 closes as decided against for promotion, with no binding test obligation.

options.label: After the Dafny step
options.description: Keep it open until the operations pass shows which clauses are observable through the API.

questions.question: T2: spec 004 (RemotePath) normalizes and rejects input in ways the axioms don't (`.`, `..`, `a/`, `//`, `\`, empty path). How should the new store-model spec relate to spec 004?

options.label: Input vs Key layering (Recommended)
options.description: Record it: spec 004 governs input strings, and RemotePath maps an accepted input onto a Key; the store-model spec governs Keys and the tree. So the library only ever addresses a subset of the model's Keys (no `.`, `..` or `\` names; the root by the store, not a path). PATH-009..011 are string operations on that Key. The "one home" claim narrows to the tree's structure.

options.label: Reopen as open decision
options.description: Make spec 004's relation BK-435's open decision again. Nothing is decided now, and the spec author settles it, possibly by amending spec 004 clauses.

options.label: Amend spec 004 to match
options.description: Decide now that spec 004's clauses conflicting with the axioms get amended (e.g. `.` and `..` as ordinary names). That is a breaking change to RemotePath and needs its own item and CHANGELOG entry.

questions.question: T1: BK-432's remaining work lands RFC-0021 Appendix A (with A.1's tree prose) as spec 003 § The store tree, while the store-model spec doesn't exist yet. Which lands first?

options.label: BK-432 first, pointer later (Recommended)
options.description: BK-432 lands Appendix A as accepted, A.1 included, unblocked on Thursday. When BK-435's spec lands, it replaces A.1's structural prose with a pointer. BK-432's entry names this, and BK-435's names the replacement as its job. The tree is stated twice only in between.

options.label: BK-432 lands A.1 as a stub
options.description: BK-432's section omits A.1's structure and says the store-model spec (BK-435) will state it. The tree is never stated twice, but spec 003 has a gap until BK-435 lands, which changes accepted RFC-0021's landing plan.

options.label: Store-model spec first
options.description: BK-435's spec lands before BK-432's section, which then points to it from the start. BK-432's resume waits on BK-435.

questions.question: Every section of the new spec (051) needs a test marked with its ID. What should those tests run against now, given flat backends can break AX-1/AX-3 until BK-432 lands?

options.label: Reference model now, backends later (Recommended)
options.description: Tests use a small pure-Python checker of the axioms, with each section's witnesses and § 5 countermodel as cases, the same idea as the Alloy check, inside pytest. A conformance test that every backend's observed tree satisfies the spec is filed for after BK-432. Every section is enforced today, but no backend is bound yet.

options.label: Model + conformance where it holds
options.description: As above, plus a conformance test across all backends now for the clauses that already hold (root is a folder, key shape, unique names, prefix closure). AX-1 and AX-3 are declared unenforced on flat backends until BK-432. Binds backends sooner, but needs per-backend exemptions.

options.label: Conformance only
options.description: No reference model: each section is tested only through backends. AX-1 and AX-3 can't be marked until BK-432, so the spec lands partial or waits.

questions.question: What does spec 051 state as sections?

options.label: Axioms + Key + key lemmas (Recommended)
options.description: One section per axiom clause (AX-1 to AX-8), one for the Key definition, and sections for the consequences a caller relies on: unique Key (L3), Key shape (L4), prefix closure (L5). Acyclicity, chain uniqueness and the trie view (D1, L1, L2, L6) stay in the research doc and the proofs.

options.label: Axioms + Key only
options.description: AX-1 to AX-8 and the Key definition. Every lemma stays in the research doc and the proofs. Smallest spec, but a caller has to derive key uniqueness and shape themselves.

options.label: Everything
options.description: Axioms, Key, and all of D1 and L1 to L6 as sections. Most complete, but it restates the proofs in prose, and each lemma needs its own test.

options.label: TREE (Recommended)
options.description: Matches RFC-0021's "the store tree" wording and spec 003's planned § The store tree, e.g. TREE-001.

options.label: MODEL
options.description: Emphasises it's the logical model, e.g. MODEL-001.

questions.question: Point 1: backends whose name equality is coarser than exact (case-insensitive or Unicode-normalizing filesystems) can't hold every tree spec 051 allows. How should #1134 handle it?

options.label: State the bound + widen BK-436 (Recommended)
options.description: Spec 051 keeps exact comparison and gains one Overview sentence: a backend that identifies names under a coarser equivalence (case folding, Unicode normalization) represents only stores whose sibling names are distinct under it. BK-436's open decision also covers measuring each backend's name equality.

options.label: Separate backlog item
options.description: Leave spec 051 as is and file a new item for backend name equivalence (Local on macOS/Windows vs S3/Azure), apart from BK-436.

options.label: Fix a normalization form
options.description: Gemini's suggestion: names compare after NFC. This changes the accepted model (it makes aliases) and needs the research doc, Alloy, Lean and RFC-0021 revisited.

questions.question: Point 3: nothing mechanical ties TREE-n to its Alloy predicate or Lean field. What should happen?

options.label: File a tooling item (Recommended)
options.description: A backlog item to add @spec TREE-n tags to the Alloy and Lean restatements and extend check_formal_trace.py to read them, as it does for Dafny. That catches a missing link, not a change in meaning. #1134 stays as it is.

options.label: Tags now, checker later
options.description: Add `-- @spec TREE-00n` comments to the Lean and Alloy files in #1134 now (no checker reads them yet), and file the checker extension.

options.label: No action
options.description: The reference-model tests plus review are the guard; record nothing.

questions.question: Point 1: backends whose name equality is coarser than exact (case-insensitive or Unicode-normalizing filesystems) can't hold every tree spec 051 allows. How should #1134 handle it?

options.label: State the bound + widen BK-436 (Recommended)
options.description: Spec 051 keeps exact comparison and gains one Overview sentence: a backend that identifies names under a coarser equivalence (case folding, Unicode normalization) represents only stores whose sibling names are distinct under it. BK-436's open decision also covers measuring each backend's name equality.
